body:
You are a dialogue and narration writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown, no code fences, no preamble, no commentary after) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, in the exact format asked.

SETTING OF THIS TASK: the catacombs under Castle Ravenloft, where the old house of von Zarovich buries its dead in rows of iron-gated crypts, each with a name over the gate. The party is level 10. Count Strahd von Zarovich is the vampire lord of the castle. The crypts are orderly, cold and almost tender; the horror is how long everything has waited. A few of the book's crypts are comic (a chef with a bell, a knight who tripped on his own sword, a rich man's painted gold coins). Those keep their joke deadpan and never wink at the player.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, not from jokes about the horror. Where a scene is sad, let it be sad. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Do not invent other named people than the ones given. Do not use em-dashes (use commas, colons or full stops). Do not use semicolons more than once in a line. Plain words a voice actor can read aloud.

NARRATOR STYLE (second person, present tense, one or two sentences). Samples from the existing game, to match voice, length and rhythm:
- A bronze plaque, green with age: the old king's champion, who never lost a fight. It lists the men he killed. It takes up the whole plaque.
- Over the foot of the stair, two words cut deep and plain: HE RESTS. Nothing about peace.
- The lord of the house in marble, seated, a wolf at his feet. The sculptor made him kinder than he is, and the stone has not forgiven either of them.
- Words are cut over the stair: the house keeps its dead. Someone has added, below it, in a smaller hand: and its dead keep the house.
Carved words are written in CAPITALS inside the sentence, as in the samples.

TASK: write ONE Narrator line for each slot below, in the format
SLOT_ID: the line
(one line per slot, nothing else). Each line is at most 32 words unless the slot says otherwise. Slots marked "epitaph" describe the words carved over a crypt gate or lintel: quote the carved words in CAPITALS, then add at most one short Narrator sentence. Never repeat a joke or a sentence shape between slots.

CRYPTS (each is a small chamber behind an iron gate; the party looks at things from outside and inside):

TASHA_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Tasha Petrovna, servant and companion to the royal household. Faithful, plain, loved.
TASHA_SUN: examine the sun painted gold on the ceiling of Tasha's crypt. It gives off a faint warmth and a real glow; the undead cannot bear to stand under it (say so plainly, in the Narrator's voice).
TROISKY_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of King Troisky, the Three-Faced King, who ruled in a helm with three faces.
TROISKY_HELM: examine the slab: a helm with three carved faces rests on the dead king's chest, and the faces' mouths are open. Hint (do not state) that lifting it would be a mistake.
TROISKY_GAS: a trap fires when someone steps on the slab's step: green gas hisses from the three mouths. One or two sentences.
ERICK_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Sir Erick Vonderbucks, a knight whose family had money.
ERICK_GOLD: examine his body: he lies dipped entirely in gold, like a statue, eyes and all. Deadpan.
BASCAL_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Bascal Ofenheiss, "Chef Deluxe", the house's cook.
BASCAL_BELL: examine a small silver bell hung on a chain beside the sarcophagus, with words engraved on it. Hint that it should not be rung.
BASCAL_FIRE: a trap fires when someone rings the bell: fire sweeps across the whole crypt. One or two sentences.
EISGLAZE_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Baron Eisglaze Drüf, a baron remembered for his coldness.
EISGLAZE_MOLD: examine the slab, thickly covered in brown mold. The air around it is far colder than the rest of the catacombs, because the mold feeds on warmth. Mention that fire would clear it.
EISGLAZE_COLD: a trap fires when someone steps near the mold: the cold sucks the heat out of them. One or two sentences.
CRYPT31_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of a crypt that has no name, only a boast about wealth. The walls inside are painted with gold coins.
CRYPT31_PIT: a trap fires: the painted floor tilts and gives way over a pit of spikes. One or two sentences.
KLUTZ_EPITAPH: epitaph over the gate of Sir Klutz Tripalotsky, a knight who tripped and fell on his own sword.
KLUTZ_SWORD: examine the skeleton: a sword stands through its breastplate. Deadpan; the party cannot help seeing how it happened.
result:
TASHA_EPITAPH: The lintel reads: TASHA PETROVNA, WHO STAYED. Someone has polished the iron gate long after the rest of the hallway went to rust.
TASHA_SUN: A gold sun painted on the vault still gives off a real, quiet warmth. No dead thing that walks could bear to stand beneath it.
TROISKY_EPITAPH: Deep letters over the bars read: KING TROISKY THE THREE-FACED, WHO WATCHED THREE WAYS AND DIED IN BED.
TROISKY_HELM: A bronze helm with three carved faces sits on the dead king's breast, all three mouths ajar. A thin wire runs from the chin-strap into the stone.
TROISKY_GAS: The step sinks under your boot. Green gas hisses from all three mouths of the helm, thick and sweet.
ERICK_EPITAPH: Gilt letters above the gate announce: SIR ERICK VONDERBUCKS, PAID IN FULL. Even the full stop has been leafed in gold.
ERICK_GOLD: They dipped him in gold before they laid him down, eyelids, fingernails and all. It must have taken three men to carry him.
BASCAL_EPITAPH: Carved in a neat kitchen hand: BASCAL OFENHEISS, CHEF DELUXE, WHO FED THIS HOUSE. The stone still smells faintly of lard and smoke.
BASCAL_BELL: A little silver bell hangs on a chain beside the coffin, engraved: DO NOT RING FOR SERVICE. The clapper is blackened with old soot.
BASCAL_FIRE: The bell gives one bright chime, and a sheet of fire roars out from under the lid to fill the vault.
EISGLAZE_EPITAPH: Cut into frost-split stone: BARON EISGLAZE DRÜF, COLD IN LIFE, COLDER AFTER.
EISGLAZE_MOLD: Thick brown mold furs the slab, drinking every drop of warmth from the air until your breath hangs white. Only a good fire would burn it off.
EISGLAZE_COLD: The air snaps shut around you as the mold drinks the heat straight out of your skin. Your fingers go numb on the hilt.
CRYPT31_EPITAPH: No name is cut above the arch, only: WE KNEW HOW TO KEEP IT. Beyond the bars, someone has painted gold coins all over the damp plaster.
CRYPT31_PIT: The painted flagstones tip under your weight and drop away. Iron spikes wait at the bottom of the dark.
KLUTZ_EPITAPH: Over the gate, cut with reluctant honesty: SIR KLUTZ TRIPALOTSKY, HE FELL ON HIS OWN SWORD. It does not sound like he meant to.
KLUTZ_SWORD: His broadsword stands straight up through the breastplate, hilt to the floor and point through the spine. His boot-heels are still hooked together.
